title: feat: LinkedIn description enrichment + paginated found-jobs MCP resource
body:
## Summary

Two independent fixes for the Agent/MCP job-discovery surface, bundled into one PR by request:

### 1. LinkedIn post-discovery description enrichment (#1114, LinkedIn slice)
- LinkedIn search results never carry a description (`LinkedInJobsApiClient` always writes `Some(String::new())`), so LinkedIn postings scored title-only forever. The other 6 boards named in #1114 have no per-URL detail resolver at all (confirmed by inspection) and are out of scope here.
- A best-effort background pass, spawned after `autopilot_run`'s `record_run` call, resolves each still-blank LinkedIn posting via the existing `scraping::scrape_url::resolve` single-URL resolver, paced through LinkedIn's existing shared rate limiter, and writes any real description back through the existing `scrape_update_description` mechanism (#1109's write-back fix).
- Capped at 15 fetches/run; a per-URL failure is logged and never fails the run itself.
- **Review history**: `scraping-applier-expert` caught a CRITICAL — `merge_found_jobs` treated LinkedIn's `Some("")` blank sentinel as "known," silently wiping every enriched description back to blank on the next scrape and re-fetching it forever. Fixed with a `description_is_blank`-aware merge guard, mutation-tested. The pre-push architecture gate then caught a real L2→L3 layer violation in the fix (Tauri types/command calls leaking into an `autopilot_helpers` module); fixed by splitting pure logic from Tauri orchestration across the existing layer boundary this crate already uses for `rerank.rs`/`best_matches.rs`.

### 2. Paginated `found-jobs` Agent/MCP resource (#1115)
- No Agent/MCP command could enumerate an autopilot's `found_jobs` — every real autopilot (459 KB–1.87 MB) exceeds the MCP bridge's 256 KiB response cap, and the only alternative (`autopilot_best_matches`) is a hardcoded top-100 across all autopilots combined with no parameters.
- New read-only, paginated `found-jobs` resource (CLI verb, MCP tool, `agent.query` resource): `{autopilotId, limit?, cursor?} → {jobs, nextCursor, total, autopilotId, autopilotName}`.
- **Review history**: `agent-cli-reviewer` and `tauri-security-reviewer` both reviewed in parallel (new data-exposing surface). Two HIGH findings from `agent-cli-reviewer`, converging with the security review's MEDIUM: a numeric `cursor` was silently coerced to "absent," resetting pagination to page 1 without any signal; and the page-size guard bounded characters, not bytes, so the real worst-case page was ~2.5 MB, not the ~168 KB either review first estimated — reachable via ordinary non-ASCII postings, not just adversarial ones. Fixed with a byte-budget trim (drops rows until the serialized page fits, cursor reflects rows actually kept) and correct `Value`-variant cursor parsing.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test --lib` — 5265 passed, 0 failed
- [x] `cargo test --test architecture` — 18/18 passed
- [x] `cargo test --test mcp_smoke` — fixed a hardcoded tool-list assertion that hadn't been extended for the new resource
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- [x] `cargo deny check` / `cargo machete` — clean

title: Agent/MCP cannot enumerate Autopilot.found_jobs — no pagination, all 8 autopilots exceed the 256 KiB MCP result cap
body:
## Summary
No Agent/MCP-exposed command can enumerate an autopilot's complete `found_jobs` list. `autopilot_get`/`autopilot_list` return the full, unbounded `Autopilot` record, and every one of the app's 8 current autopilots (459 KB–1.87 MB) exceeds the MCP bridge's own `MCP_RESULT_MAX_BYTES = 256 * 1024` cap (`extension_bridge/agent_cli/mcp.rs:622`), so both commands are refused outright (`result_too_large`) for every autopilot tested. The only Agent/MCP-reachable read path, `autopilot_best_matches`, is a separate cross-autopilot ranked projection hard-capped at `BEST_MATCHES_CAP = 100` (`commands/autopilot/best_matches.rs:32`) — a constant the command's own doc comment calls "a payload guard, not the selection rule," and the command takes **no parameters at all**, so a caller-supplied `limit` is silently ignored.

This is **not** a database limitation and **not** a GUI limitation — see below.

## What we verified (source-referenced)
- `useAutopilots()` → `api.autopilot.list()` (`renderer/services/use-autopilot/use-autopilot.ts:29-36`) loads the full `Autopilot[]`, each with its complete `foundJobs` array, into the renderer.
- `AutopilotCard` receives the whole `Autopilot` object as a prop and renders the full `foundJobs` array (filtered only for cluster-canonical rows) into a plain scrollable `max-h-64` div — `renderer/features/autopilot/components/AutopilotCard/index.tsx:248-251, 715-717`. There is no frontend pagination anywhere in this component.
- Backend `autopilot_list`/`autopilot_get` (`commands/autopilot.rs:101-117`) take no filter, offset, cursor, or board-scope parameter — full record or nothing.
- `autopilot_best_matches` (`commands/autopilot.rs:759-761`, `commands/autopilot/best_matches.rs:29-32`) takes zero arguments; `BEST_MATCHES_CAP = 100` is a hardcoded constant with no request-side override.
- The Agent/MCP bridge's transport cap, `MCP_RESULT_MAX_BYTES = 256 * 1024` (`extension_bridge/agent_cli/mcp.rs:622`), applies to every JSON-RPC response regardless of command.
- All 8 existing autopilots were individually probed via `autopilot_get` through the MCP bridge; every one was refused as `result_too_large`, with the bridge's own reported payload size:

| Autopilot | Payload size | Over the 256 KiB cap by |
|---|---|---|
| Business Development Milan | 1,876,914 B | 7.3× |
| Digital Marketing Milan | 1,699,992 B | 6.6× |
| International Business Milan | 1,200,893 B | 4.7× |
| Market Research Turin | 998,165 B | 3.9× |
| Market Research Milan | 902,821 B | 3.5× |
| Business Development Turin | 767,099 B | 3.0× |
| International Business Turin | 511,653 B | 2.0× |
| Digital Marketing Turin | 459,486 B | 1.8× |

The smallest of the 8 is still 1.8× over the cap.

## The actual gap
The GUI reaches the complete `found_jobs` data because it talks to `autopilot_get`/`autopilot_list` over Tauri's native IPC, which has no comparable size ceiling. An Agent/MCP caller hits the exact same unbounded commands, but through a bridge that enforces a 256 KiB response cap with no narrower alternative. There is no pagination, cursor, per-board filter, or windowed slice exposed anywhere in the `autopilot` command surface for `found_jobs` — confirmed by reading every `#[tauri::command]` in `commands/autopilot.rs`.

To be precise about the data in question: this is existing autopilot-found job data that is accessible to the GUI but not currently enumerable through the Agent/MCP interface, because the existing read commands return unbounded records that exceed the MCP transport response limit. It is not junk, not unverified, and not inaccessible from the database — the database and the GUI both already have it.

## Why this matters
An Agent/MCP-driven quality-cleanup or qualification pass over the job pool can only reach the top 100 rows `autopilot_best_matches` ranks across all autopilots combined. For a pool that currently sits at several hundred qualifying postings, everything below that ranked top-100 is invisible to any Agent/MCP caller today, even though the GUI user can already scroll through it per-search. This caps how much of the discovered pool can ever be reviewed, deduplicated, or verified through the Agent/MCP surface, independent of pool size or score quality.

## Proposed fix
Add a bounded, paginated, read-only command — not a change to `MCP_RESULT_MAX_BYTES`. Raising the global transport cap would let any command return arbitrarily large payloads and wouldn't address the underlying lack of pagination; a dedicated paginated endpoint is the narrower, safer fix.

Suggested shape (illustrative, not prescriptive):

```
autopilot_list_found_jobs
  req: { autopilotId: string, limit: number, cursor?: string }
  → { jobs: FoundJobSlice[], nextCursor: string | null, autopilotId, autopilotName }
```

- `FoundJobSlice` should carry only what a caller needs for qualification/dismissal: title, company, url, location, source/board, description (when present), postedAt/foundAt, score/scoreSource/scoreProvisional, trust assessment, and whatever identifier `scrape_persist_job`'s dismissal path already keys on — not the full `FoundJob` record if that carries anything heavier.
- Page size should be chosen so a full page stays comfortably under 256 KiB for the richest existing records (the 1.87 MB autopilot's average per-job size suggests a page of roughly 100-200 jobs, but that should be verified against real data rather than assumed).
- Cursor can be a plain index/offset into the stored `found_jobs` order, or an opaque token — whichever matches an existing pagination convention already used elsewhere in the codebase, if one exists, rather than inventing a new pattern.

### Requirements
1. Read-only — no mutation of jobs, applications, generations, or application status.
2. Deterministic pagination — repeated calls with the same cursor return the same slice (barring concurrent discovery).
3. Lets the complete `found_jobs` array of one autopilot be traversed to completion via repeated calls.
4. Each returned job carries enough to identify its source autopilot/search.
5. Every response stays safely under the MCP transport limit, including for the largest current autopilot (~1.87 MB full record).
6. Purely additive — `autopilot_get`, `autopilot_list`, `autopilot_best_matches`, and existing GUI behavior are unchanged.
7. Returns only the fields an Agent/MCP caller plausibly needs, not the full internal `FoundJob` shape if it carries anything beyond that.

## Acceptance criteria
- Agent/MCP can request page 1 of a given autopilot's found jobs.
- Following the returned cursor yields page 2, page 3, etc., until `nextCursor` is `null`.
- The full `found_jobs` collection of every one of the 8 current autopilots (including the ~1.87 MB one) can be enumerated this way without any single response exceeding the MCP result cap.
- No existing application, job, or generation state changes as a side effect of calling it.
- `autopilot_get`, `autopilot_list`, `autopilot_best_matches`, and the GUI's own found-jobs rendering behave exactly as before.

title: No automatic post-discovery description enrichment for search-only boards (LinkedIn + 6 others)
body:
## Summary
No automatic post-discovery enrichment pass exists for boards whose search results never include a description — LinkedIn's free tier plus six others (TheMuse, Comeet, Breezy, BambooHR, Pinpoint, Rippling, per the maintainer's own comment at `commands/autopilot.rs` — see below). This is a distinct, narrower remaining gap from #1105, which is closed and correctly scoped to *signaling* honesty, not content fetching.

## What's already fixed (not being re-litigated)
#1105 (closed, PR #1109) fixed the score/trust dishonesty around missing content: `score_provisional` now fires for any title-only-scored posting, and a `DescriptionUnavailable` trust flag caps confidence below High. Confirmed still correct and unchanged in current `main`.

## What already exists (pull-based, manual only)
`scraping/scrape_url::resolve` → `try_linkedin` (`scraping/scrape_url/mod.rs:994`) can fetch a real LinkedIn description for a single URL, using an authenticated client + real selectors. It's invoked from exactly two places, both requiring an explicit action: `scrape_url`/`scrape_resolve_url` (`commands/scrape.rs:369,597`) and the browser-extension's "import this job" flow (`extension_bridge/import_flow.rs:233,255,263`). No caller anywhere invokes it automatically after autopilot discovery — confirmed via a repo-wide search for any background/queue/worker/scheduled description-fetch mechanism (zero matches beyond unrelated `backfill_*` functions for geocoding, salary, application linking, etc. — none touch job descriptions).

## The actual gap
`scraping/linkedin/api_client/mod.rs:303` — every LinkedIn search-result posting is built with `description: Some(String::new()), // Will be filled in background`. No such background process exists. The maintainer's own comment on the `no_jd_text` flag (added in the #1109 fix, `commands/autopilot.rs` ~line 845) confirms this precisely:

> "Six other boards never populate a search-result description either (no detail-enrichment pass runs between the initial scrape and this projection for any of them): TheMuse, Comeet, Breezy, BambooHR, Pinpoint, Rippling."

Same statement is echoed in `docs/knowledge/matching-algorithm.md`. So this isn't a LinkedIn-only complaint, and it isn't disputed that the gap exists — it's already documented in the codebase, just not tracked as an actionable item anywhere I could find.

## Why this matters for bulk/automated qualification
A caller (the app's own UI, or an Agent/MCP consumer) can correct one specific posting by hand — call the pull-based resolver, then `scrape_update_description` (fixed in #1109 to write through to `Autopilot.found_jobs`). But there is no way to reliably qualify or tailor materials against the *bulk* pool for these 7 boards without either manually opening every single posting first, or accepting a title-only match with no real content behind it. For a pool with hundreds of postings, most from LinkedIn, this is the practical ceiling on automated qualification today.

## Smallest reasonable fix scope
Reuse the existing per-board resolvers (`try_linkedin` and whatever equivalents exist for the other 6 boards) rather than writing new scraping logic — trigger one resolve pass per newly-discovered posting shortly after discovery (rate-limit-aware), writing the result back through the same path `scrape_update_description` already uses to reach `Autopilot.found_jobs`. Not a scraper rewrite; the extraction logic already exists and already works some of the time.

_Filed from an Agent/MCP-based QA pass, as a distinct follow-up to the closed #1105 — that issue's signaling fix is confirmed correct and is not being reopened._

title: [POC-2] Review Agent-Initiated Browser Navigation
body:
## POC-2 — Technical Review Request

### Scope
Agent-initiated navigation only:
`applications_open → open a stored application's job URL in a new background browser tab via the existing extension bridge`

No form filling and no submission capability were added or attempted.

### Implementation status
POC-2 is implemented in an isolated local worktree and has never been pushed.

Implemented:
- `NAVIGATE_REQUEST` / `NAVIGATE_RESULT` protocol
- Rust wire constants and shared TypeScript protocol types
- `applications_open` command with `Effect::Reversible`
- bridge correlation registry
- extension handler using `browser.tabs.create({ url, active: false })`

### Verified
- TypeScript typecheck: clean
- Extension tests: 588/588 passing across 14 files
- Zero test regressions

### Unverified / blocker
Rust/Tauri compilation could not be completed.

Root cause was confirmed precisely using `vswhere.exe`: Visual Studio Build Tools 2019 is installed, but the C++/MSVC workload was never installed. `cl.exe` and `link.exe` are absent from the machine.

Therefore this is currently a machine environment blocker, not evidence that the POC-2 Rust source changes fail to compile.

Because the binary could not be built, the real E2E test:
`Agent → App → Extension → browser.tabs.create({ active:false })`
could not be executed.

### Safety design
The implementation remains intentionally constrained:
- HTTPS-only
- Requested URL must exactly match the application's stored `job_url`
- Opens a new background tab with `active:false`
- Does not touch the user's active tab
- No generic browser-control API
- No `applications_submit` capability
- No automatic form submission
- `submitDetected` remains observational only

The intended workflow stops at `READY_TO_SUBMIT`; the user manually performs the final Submit action.

### Isolation
Nothing has been:
- deployed to the live app
- deployed to the live extension
- pushed
- merged
- submitted as a PR
- installed on the system
- changed in system configuration

### Review requested
Please review the POC-2 architecture and security model, especially:
1. `applications_open` design
2. App → Extension navigation protocol
3. Exact `job_url` matching and HTTPS validation
4. Background-tab behavior via `tabs.create({ active:false })`
5. Absence of any Agent-side submission capability
6. Whether this architecture is appropriate to proceed to build verification and E2E testing

No further implementation should be started until this review is complete.
